verdict.rationale: Qodo's docs describe a PR reviewer that looks at the full codebase rather than just the diff. They say it surfaces issues that matter, ranked by severity, while avoiding low-signal feedback, and that it catches breaking changes that diff-only tools miss. That is a first-party claim to substantive rather than stylistic review. However, the docs never name logic errors, race conditions or edge-case bugs as finding types, and no hands-on evidence shows it catching real bugs. One community user switching to another tool is not a concrete counter-example. Missing for 10: documented detection of logic errors, race conditions and broken edge cases; independent or hands-on corroboration of bug-finding accuracy.

support.subject: As a developer, the reviewer catches real bugs in my PR — logic errors, race conditions, broken edge cases — not just style nits

citations.quote: The review focuses on surfacing issues that matter, explaining why they matter, and helping developers resolve them efficiently, without overwhelming you with low-signal feedback.
catching breaking changes, spec gaps, and design deviations that diff-only tools miss.
every finding states what needs attention, why it matters, and how to fix it, ranked by severity
